name: Common Myanmar Myanglish Normalization Lexicon
description: A practical context-aware mapping for informal Burmese written with Latin characters, especially compressed chat spelling. Myanglish is non-standard, so many forms have multiple valid spellings and some forms are ambiguous.
important_notes: Myanglish has no official spelling standard.
Writers frequently omit vowels, duplicate consonants for emphasis, and mix English with Burmese.
Do not normalize a token only from spelling when it is marked ambiguous; use neighboring words and sentence structure.
Final particles such as lrr/lar, ll/le, tl/te, bu/woo, naw, lay and lr may carry grammatical meaning and should not be discarded.
Case is usually irrelevant in chat: Br, BR and br often represent the same token.
Repeated letters often carry emphasis rather than a different lexical meaning: lrrr, wooow, nawrr.
Spaces are unreliable. The same phrase may appear joined, separated, or partially abbreviated.

normalization_rules.description: Lowercase Latin text for dictionary lookup, while retaining the original form for reconstruction.
When lookup fails, try collapsing excessive repeated final letters: lrrrr -> lrr, woooo -> woo, nawrrr -> naw.

normalization_rules.example: kg lrr -> ကောင်းလား

recommended_pipeline: Normalize obvious emphasis/repetition only if direct lookup fails.
Try longest phrase matches before token-level matches.
Use composition patterns for unmatched sequences.
For ambiguous tokens, score interpretations using neighboring tokens and grammatical position.
Retain unknown English words as English; Burmese chat often code-switches.
Do not hallucinate Burmese script for unknown names, usernames, acronyms, or slang.
Return multiple candidates with confidence when context cannot resolve an ambiguity.
